root_cause_label: Position Desync from Elevation-Ignorant BFS Causes Infinite Loop
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent wrote nine solution versions all sharing the same fatal flaw of unconditionally updating the internal position after every move command regardless of whether the engine accepted the move, causing position desynchronization, phantom BFS paths, and infinite loops that prevented any trial from completing.
t_err_evidence: implementation updates position blindly (assumes moves always succeed), desynchronizing internal coordinates; omits pickup/drop stair-building logic
t_commit_evidence: From step 25 onward, every rewrite (steps 30, 34, 35, 39, 40, 44, 45, 47, 49) repeats the same unconditional position update pattern. The agent never implemented move-success verification or an alternative approach that avoids position desync, locking in the failing pattern from the first implementation attempt.
t_surface_evidence: Turn limit exceeded (repeated 20+ times) — solution never reaches gold
trigger_explanation: The agent acted on the unverified assumption that all move commands would succeed, unconditionally updating this.pos after each direction command. The engine's z() function silently rejects moves where |cell.level - u.level| > 1, but the agent never checked the return value or compared the next cell observation to confirm movement. This false premise about move success caused the internal map and BFS planning to operate from incorrect positions throughout all nine solution versions.
forewarning_evidence: ion(cell) { ... return action; }; } EOF — file content unexpectedly echoed to terminal instead of silent creation
